summary: Throughput collapse during scheduled QA spike — asymmetric routing caused GPU stripe contention
description:
Issue summary: BrightDesk reports a sustained drop in end-to-end throughput for their reserved pool during a scheduled QA job window on 2026-03-13. The pool experienced a p50 throughput collapse (~35% drop) and p99 latency spikes. Impact: customer-facing inference pipelines falling behind SLA-backed throughput commitments; retries and client timeouts observed.

Observed window: 2026-03-13 09:40—10:25 UTC (customer local: 05:40—06:25).

Initial hypothesis: a routing imbalance after a lightweight router release caused uneven distribution of short-burst requests to a subset of GPUs, creating persistent stripe contention and kernel queue serialization on those devices. This resulted in effective GPU starvation for other tenants on the pool and triggered tight autoscaler oscillation attempts, which failed to rebalance quickly enough due to min-capacity constraints.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use dedicated pool with at least 8 GPUs and min_capacity=6.
2) Replay short, high-frequency QA streams (avg tokens per request: 16, client-side concurrency: 120) with a routing key that was recently changed in the router release.
3) Observe that >60% of requests hash to 2/8 GPUs for ~20 minute window.
4) Watch per-GPU kernel queue depth and nvlink/pci counters — hot GPUs show sustained kernel queue depth > 50, frequent enqueue latency >15ms.
5) Autoscaler attempts to scale but nodes are pinned due to placement fragmentation and don't drain quickly, leaving throughput degraded.

Expected behavior: router evenly spreads short streams across GPUs; autoscaler scales smoothly to absorb transient load without persistent per-GPU saturation.
logs:
Relevant logs extracted:
- router-prod (2026-03-13T09:39:51Z): INFO routing: hash_seed=0x7a2a changed -> new_hash_fn=v2
- router-prod (2026-03-13T09:40:03Z): WARN routing: 62% of requests to pool-id=brd-01 routed to host-gpu-03,host-gpu-04
- serving-runtime (2026-03-13T09:41:10Z): WARN kernel-queue: gpu=3 queue_depth=58 enqueue_ms=18.7
- autoscaler (2026-03-13T09:41:45Z): INFO scaleattempt: desired=8 current=6 reason=high_queue_depth
- kube-events (2026-03-13T09:42:30Z): WARN pod-drain: host-gpu-03 stuck in Terminating due to local-checkpoint-writer
- dmesg (host-gpu-03): [timestamp] WARNING: gpu_mem_reclaim: triggered heavy page reclaim

Attached traces and flamegraphs linked in Confluence page (internal).
investigation_notes:
Timeline & actions so far:
- 09:40: router release v2 (hotfix) rolled to prod in us-east with a small change to request hashing logic to avoid a rare collision.
- 09:40—09:55: immediate imbalance observed; routing telemetry shows skew where 2 GPUs received disproportionate short-streams.
- 09:42—09:50: serving-runtime metrics on hot GPUs show kernel queue serialization and increased enqueue latency. NVLink/pci counters show elevated PCIe write stalls on host-gpu-03/04.
- 09:45: autoscaler increased desired capacity but several nodes couldn't be scheduled because of fragmentary HBM allocations (post-drain leftover checkpoints).
- 09:50: Support temporarily flipped router to legacy hash_fn (rollback) and set routing weight overrides for pool brd-01 -> immediate reduction in skew within 3 minutes.

Hypotheses: (1) Hash function change created deterministic skew for specific routing keys used by BrightDesk QA client, (2) Short-burst workload characteristics create high kernel queue churn on affected GPUs, exposing a driver-level memory reclaim behavior that increases enqueue latency, (3) Autoscaler reaction was muted by node drain/placement friction.

Next investigative steps: collect full per-GPU kernel queue traces, correlate with NVLink/PCIe stalls and per-tenant request traces; reproduce with local replay harness. Engineering owners: Diego (serving-runtime), Priya (router), Len (autoscaler).

resolution:
Mitigation performed: rolled back router hashing change for us-east and applied routing weight override to spread load; drained and reprovisioned two hot hosts to clear checkpoint leftovers; autoscaler guard added to increase min_capacity during short-stream floods.

Permanent fix: Router PR #1234 introduces per-pool salting and distribution tests to prevent low-entropy key bias; merged 2026-03-14 and canaryed in us-east. Autoscaler follow-up PR adds faster drain/replace heuristics and a placement resilience check (github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/1789).

Customer impact: BrightDesk experienced ~45 minutes of degraded throughput affecting scheduled QA pipelines. No customer data loss.

Follow-ups / action items:
- Runbook: update DedicatedRoutingSkew runbook with detection thresholds and automated rollback (owner: Support ops).
- Alerting: add a Console alert for per-pool routing entropy < 0.5 and per-GPU kernel queue depth > 40 (owner: Observability).
- Postmortem: schedule cross-team postmortem next week (owner: SRE).
